title: Universal purification dynamics of monitored Clifford circuits
authors: Beatrice Magni, Federico Gerbino, Xhek Turkeshi, Andrea De Luca
abstract: Quantum circuits under sufficiently weak monitoring purify on a timescale $T_P$ exponentially long in the system size. This slowness underlies a universal purification dynamics, whose quantitative description has so far required the replica trick, with a delicate analytic continuation. We show that monitored Clifford circuits on $L$ qudits of prime dimension $q$ bypass this construction entirely: in the scaling limit at fixed $x = t/T_P(L)$, purification reduces to the Markovian decay of the density-matrix rank, an exactly solvable death process descending from infinity. We compute the full scaling functions in compact form: all Rényi entropies collapse onto a universal curve $\langle S(x) \rangle$. Exact stabilizer simulations at $q=2,3,5$ confirm the predictions, with no fitting parameter for the global model and $T_P$ as the only fitted scale for local brick-wall circuits. Also, the replica problem amounts to a tilted version of the same Markov process, in agreement with exact computations from the Clifford commutant. Finally, the quantization of the rank leaves two hallmarks that distinguish Clifford dynamics from generic monitored circuits: the entropy fluctuations saturate at short scaled times $x\to0$ to an $O(1)$ variance, instead of vanishing, and observables develop a temporal modulation periodic in $\log_q x$, which cannot be captured by the replica approach.
summary: This work analyzes the purification of monitored Clifford circuits by showing the dynamics simplify dramatically compared to generic systems. The process reduces to a pure-death Markov chain whose scaling functions are universal and exactly solvable. This bypasses complex mathematical machinery like the replica trick, offering deep insights into quantum information decay rates.
main_problem: The paper investigates the universal dynamics of quantum state purification for monitored Clifford circuits, aiming to bypass complex mathematical tools like the replica trick.
main_result: For these specific circuits, purification reduces to an exactly solvable death process governing the decay of the density matrix rank, leading to universal scaling functions for Rényi entropies.
method: The analysis maps the dynamics onto a pure-death Markov process and uses techniques involving moment generating functions, Laplace transforms, and analyzing periodic modulations in the scaling limit.
model_or_system: The system is monitored quantum many-body dynamics on Clifford circuits acting on L qudits of prime dimension q. The evolution involves alternating unitary steps (random Clifford elements) and projective measurements of Pauli strings.
key_observables: Rényi entropies ($\langle S(x) angle$), purity ($\langle P(x) angle$), the decay rate of the density-matrix rank, entropy fluctuations, and temporal modulations periodic in $\log_q x$.
important_parameters: The purification time $T_P$ (exponentially long), the scaled time $x = t/T_P$, and the qudit dimension $q$ (especially prime dimensions).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on taking specific scaling limits ($L 	o \infty, x 	o 0$) and comparing results derived from integer moments versus analytic continuation methods.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the data collapse of $\langle S(x) angle$ and $1 - \langle P(x) angle$ onto universal curves for various qudit dimensions ($q=2, 3, 5$), and show log-periodic modulations in entropy.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the reduction to a death process (Chunk 1), deriving the master equation and solving it via moment generating functions (Chunk 2), then analyzing the fine structure of the small-$x$ limit, including log-periodicity (Chunk 3), and finally rigorously characterizing the variance and moments in the $q 	o \infty$ limit (Chunk 4).
why_interesting: The finding that a complex quantum process simplifies to an exactly solvable classical death process is highly valuable for understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in open quantum systems, providing concrete analytical tools beyond standard replica methods.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
